title: What-if: a chosen decision re-scored under other numbers without refitting, and how far each number can move (34.3)
request: The owner asked to finish Phase 10 without stopping. The plan (docs/guides/PHASE10_ABILITIES_PLAN.md, 34.3) asks for a what-if that re-scores a chosen decision under changed costs, values, capacity or base rate with no refit, and a sensitivity table of which change moves the decision.
spec: what_if and sensitivity in dclab_core/decide.py, on top of 34.1's choose_operating_point (which gains row weights for a changed base rate); every answer says what was not refitted.
plan: a changed number: choose again on the same out-of-fold scores with the new spec
a changed base rate: weight cases by the new rate over the old and non-cases likewise, no refit
the old decision kept under the new numbers, and the regret of not changing
a sensitivity table: each stated number times 0.25 to 4, where the share moves
tests against a fresh choice and a resampled table; review; fix

decisions.decision: A base rate change reweights the out-of-fold rows instead of resampling them
decisions.why: it is exact for the expected value under prior shift and needs no random draw; a resampled table only checks it

decisions.decision: The old decision is kept as the very rows it acted on, not as its threshold
decisions.why: a threshold re-applied under new costs or after rounding acts on other rows than the decision did

decisions.decision: With a value per row, every value scales together (value_scale) and a single value per case is refused
decisions.why: the core reads the row values, so a changed single value would silently change nothing

decisions.decision: Weighted rows choose a point only: no bootstrap, no entities, no holdout
decisions.why: those read rows, not weights; weighting them all is a larger change than a what-if needs

change: dclab_core/decide.py (WHAT_IF_TERMS, NOT_REFITTED, _rate_weights, what_if, sensitivity; choose_operating_point takes weights and divides by their total); tests/test_core_decide_whatif.py (new); version 0.108.0 with 34.2.

findings.defect: keeping the old decision re-applied its rounded threshold and dropped the rows tied at it
findings.scenario: scores on a grid of sevenths, a what-if that changed nothing: the old decision acted on 0.282 of rows, the kept one on 0.146, with a regret of 1.66 per row made up
findings.cause: the threshold in the answer is rounded to six digits; rounding up leaves the tied rows below it
findings.fix: the kept decision takes the same count of rows by the old ranking
findings.impact: a person asking whether to change their decision would be shown a regret that does not exist
alternatives: keep the threshold unrounded in the answer: still wrong when the ranking itself changes

findings.defect: with a value per row, the kept decision ranked its rows with the new costs
findings.scenario: a review's cost raised from 1 to 8: the kept decision acted on 0.518 instead of 0.684, its regret shown as 0.62 instead of 1.68
findings.cause: the expected gain that ranks rows was computed with the new spec
findings.fix: the kept rows are ranked with the old spec
findings.impact: the cost of not changing the decision would be understated

findings.defect: the kept decision ignored a smaller capacity
findings.scenario: a capacity cut from 0.5 to 0.02: the kept decision acted on 0.329 of rows and its regret was negative
findings.cause: the old rows were valued as they were, over the new cap
findings.fix: the old rows are cut to the new capacity, best first, and the answer says so
findings.impact: a decision the team can no longer carry out would look better than the new one
alternatives: mark it over capacity with no regret: less useful to the person
findings.open: on tied scores a capacity cuts through a tie for the kept decision but not for the new choice, so the regret can be negative there

findings.defect: with a value per row, a changed value per case was ignored and the sensitivity said the value never matters
findings.scenario: a value column with a value per case of 50 changed to 5000: the answer after equalled the answer before
findings.cause: the core reads the row values and never the single value
findings.fix: a single value change is refused with values per row; value_scale multiplies them all and the sensitivity table uses it
findings.impact: a project valued by a column (an order's amount) would be told its decision does not depend on the value

findings.defect: with row weights only the curve used them: the intervals, the capacity flag and the value per row read rows
findings.scenario: weights for a base rate of 0.5 on 0.15 with the default bootstrap: a value of 18.43 with an interval of 4.17 to 4.79; all weights 2 doubled the value
findings.cause: the bootstrap and the summaries were written before weights existed
findings.fix: weights choose a point only (no bootstrap, entities or holdout); the value divides by the total weight; shares and the capacity flag are weighted
findings.impact: any later caller passing weights would get intervals that do not hold their own point
alternatives: weight the bootstrap too: a larger change for no current caller

measurements.name: a changed cost against a fresh choice, a base rate against a resampled table
measurements.gate: a changed cost gives exactly a fresh choice's point; a base rate's share within 0.02 of choosing again on a resampled table
measurements.result: the same point exactly; for a base rate of 0.15 moved to 0.05 the reviewer measured 0.117 against 0.114 to 0.126 on ten resampled tables
limits: prior shift assumes the scores of cases and non-cases keep their shape

outcome: A chosen decision can be asked what if a cost, a value, the capacity or the base rate changes, without refitting: the new point, the old decision's very rows valued anew, the regret of not changing, and how far each number can move.
lessons: Keep a decision as the rows it acted on, never as a rounded threshold re-applied.
A what-if must refuse a change the core does not read, or it answers that nothing matters.
A new argument (weights) must reach every summary or be refused where it does not.
risks: a base rate far from the training rows' makes the reweighting rest on few rows
a person may read a what-if as a promise; the note says nothing was refitted
